Attached is a light perf snapshot from our side and the request IDs I captured. Can you confirm whether this aligns with any known incidents on your side? This is affecting key matching flows — we need a mitigation ASAP.

On Thu, Mar 11, 2027 at 9:22 AM Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Marco — we see the same on our telemetry. I'm opening an internal investigation...

Summary of what I'm seeing from the runtime side:
- Rapid working set churn on GPUs serving the Fincrest shard; sustained allocations after a high-volume burst.
- KV cache eviction rate increased sharply which created more cache misses and longer token-generation work per request.
- A subset of pods reported CUDA OOMs and restarted; those restarts trigger retry fallthroughs from the gateway which send traffic back to the pool, causing a cascade.
- Retries from clients are amplifying the problem (several 429/5xx->retries loop).

Immediate mitigation applied (09:34):
- Enabled tenant-level soft-rate-limit (throttle to 60% of usual qps) for Fincrest.
- Disabled aggressive retry fallthrough at the gateway (now returns 503 fast instead of requeueing).
- Temporarily pinned Fincrest to a lower-memory model variant while we stabilize.

I've attached a small heapdump and perf snapshot from one affected node; we'll keep these for deeper analysis.

Next: I'm going to reproduce the allocation pattern on staging to validate fragmentation hypothesis, then propose a scheduling/placement change to reduce co-tenancy pressure.

— Dev (on-call, Serving Runtime)

Subject: Re: Sudden p99 and 5xx spike this morning (Fincrest production) — postmortem/next steps

Hi all — follow-up and current status (post triage):

Root cause (summary):
- The immediate p99 surge was driven by an OOM cascade on a subset of GPU hosts serving Fincrest. The cascade started when a high-throughput job caused transient larger-than-typical sequence-lengths and memory allocations. Because of prior fragmentation (long-running mixed workloads on those hosts) allocations failed intermittently and triggered container restarts. The gateway's retry fallthrough policy requeued work onto remaining healthy hosts, which in turn increased their working set and pushed more nodes into OOM.
- Contributing factor: KV cache eviction churn increased request CPU/GPU time, and batching behavior (cold batching windows during the burst) amplified per-request cost.

What we did immediately:
- Throttled tenant, disabled retry fallthrough, pinned tenant to lower-memory variant, moved ~30% of Fincrest traffic to an isolated host-pool (best-effort Dedicated slice) for stability.
- Applied temporary scheduler change to reduce co-tenancy on affected hosts and drained the most fragmented nodes.

Action items & timeline:
1) Short-term (next 48h): automated placement policy to avoid heavily fragmented GPUs for bursty tenants; increase guarded headroom on host-pools (ETA 24h).
2) Mid-term (2–3 weeks): implement smarter retry semantics at the gateway (circuit-breaker + jittered backoff) and KV-cache grace periods to avoid synchronized mass-evictions.
3) Long-term (quarter): investigate compacting allocator and improved memory defragmentation hooks in the runtime; consider a preemptible warm pool to absorb bursts.

Customer remediation & credits:
- Dylan/Evelyn: recommend offering Fincrest a credit for the incident window and the temporary Dedicated capacity used. I'll provide a cost estimate by EOD and a one-paragraph incident summary for their compliance team.

Attachments: perf_snapshot_2027-03-11.json, heapdump_node-3-03-11.tar.gz, short SLO runbook (slo_runbook_short.pdf).

Status: Fincrest production has been stable for 20+ hours after mitigation; we'll keep monitoring.

— Dev (Serving Runtime)
